title: Yayoi Kusama, visionary painter and creator of Infinity Rooms, dies at 97
summary: David Zwirner announced the passing of Yayoi Kusama. The artist passed away from multiple organ failure at a hospital in Tokyo on August 14, 2026, at the age of 97. Kusama devoted her life to an international career as an avant-garde artist, working primarily in the visual arts while also extending her practice to performance, novels, poetry, and other forms of expression. She continued to paint until shortly before her passing, never setting aside her brush, and remained steadfast in her lifelong belief that love can save the world. David Zwirner states: It’s been one of the great privileges of my professional life to have been able to represent Yayoi Kusama’s extraordinary art for the last fifteen years. title: MARCO names Sofía Hernández Chong Cuy as first sponsored curator-at-large in Mexico
summary: The Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Monterrey (MARCO) has appointed curator and art critic Sofía Hernández Chong Cuy as its new Yolanda Santos de Hoyos Curator-at-Large, a newly created position that the museum says is the first of its kind in Mexico. The appointment, announced on August 25, marks a significant step in MARCO’s efforts to rethink how its permanent collection can be presented and interpreted, particularly in relation to the cultural complexity of northern Mexico and its connections across the U.S.-Mexico border. The position is being sponsored by Monterrey philanthropist and art collector Yolanda Santos de Hoyos. Hernández Chong Cuy, who was born in Mexicali, Baja California, in 1975, brings more than two decades of curatorial experience to the museum. title: Wolfgang Tillmans returns to Galerie Chantal Crousel with new Paris show
summary: Exactly one year after the closing of his exhibition at the Centre Pompidou and following a year at the Beaux-Arts as visiting professor, Wolfgang Tillmans returns to Galerie Chantal Crousel, extending a seamless continuous conversation with Paris. Since the 1980s, Wolfgang Tillmans has developed a practice grounded in observation and in questioning the realities he encounters. His images are composed as fragments of lived experience while demonstrating that the reality we perceive is also one we actively construct. Portraits, everyday objects, landscapes, fragments of nature, and architecture are all approached with the same degree of attention, without hierarchy – a sustained attentiveness to detail and to the conditions of perception that runs throughout the exhibition. At the core of the exhibition lies an examination of the line, which in various ways and functions, has played a major role in the artist’s practice throughout the years. Tillmans's engagement

title: New exhibition at the McNay Art Museum celebrates the innovation of visual arts in 20th-century Paris
summary: When artists from around the world flocked to Paris in the 1900s, they fostered imaginative innovation that shifted the trajectory of visual art. The McNay Art Museum celebrates the creativity that blossomed from their collaboration in “Modern Paris: A Century Begins,” on view Oct. 30, 2026-Jan. 24, 2027. The exhibition of more than 50 paintings, prints and sculptures draws exclusively from the McNay Art Museum’s permanent collection and showcases a range of artists, including Georges Braque, Marc Chagall, Henri Matisse, Amedeo Modigliani, Berthe Morisot, Pablo Picasso, Chaïm Soutine and Vincent van Gogh. The exhibition highlights Marion Koogler McNay as the Museum’s founding collector and opens with Alfred Sisley’s “The Route from Saint-Germain to Marly” (1872). title: Kim Conaty named Director of the Hood Museum of Art
summary: Kim Conaty, the Nancy and Steven Crown Family Chief Curator at the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York City, has been named the Virginia Rice Kelsey 1961s Director of the Hood Museum of Art, beginning October 27, Provost Santiago Schnell announced today. “Kim Conaty is an exceptional leader and visionary curator who understands that beauty and the arts are central to the life of a university and to our mission of forming whole persons and fostering human connections,” Schnell says. “She brings the knowledge and experience needed to lead the Hood Museum in developing its next strategic plan and continuing to shape its identity as a center for original scholarship and rich student and community engagement.” Conaty, a specialist in modern and contemporary art with a focus on drawings and prints, succeeds John Stomberg, who retired this month after a 10-year tenure during which he oversaw a $50 million

title: A dime worth 15 million times its value to be auctioned
summary: Stack’s Bowers Galleries, the oldest and most accomplished numismatic auction house, will be auctioning off a dime so rare that it made its future co-chairman a national celebrity when he was only 19. Rarities like the 1894-S dime, an American classic, have layers of desirability. Some collectors are most attracted to a tiny population, some to an elite reputation, some to an oft-recited history. Only 24 examples were struck with a net mintage of just 21 coins after three were assayed and only nine specimens are positively confirmed to still exist. Market appearances are usually few and far between, as 1894-S dimes have traditionally spent years, if not decades, in tightly held collections. Since 2005, only five 1894-S dimes have been sold at auction, ranging from $1.3 million to $2.16 million. This particular example has an estimated value of $1.5 million. title: New Orleans Museum of Art announces major gift of Isamu Noguchi sculpture
summary: The New Orleans Museum of Art (NOMA) announced today that the Besthoff family has gifted a monumental work by sculptor Isamu Noguchi. Titled Mississippi Fountain (also known as The Mississippi), the work was created for what has long been known as K&B Plaza. Designed by architect Gordon Bunshaft for Skidmore, Owings, and Merrill and built in 1961–62, the building is one of New Orleans’s most prominent examples of midcentury modern architecture. Mississippi Fountain is Noguchi’s poetic distillation of the river as a symbol of a vast American landscape, of its elemental power, and of relationships between earth, water, movement, and culture. The sculpture has been located at K&B Plaza (formerly the John Hancock Insurance Company headquarters) since its construction. NOMA has begun preparations to install the work

title: Christie's to auction Au Bak Ling Collection Volume III in Hong Kong
summary: Continuing the remarkable series of live auctions at Christie’s that has captivated collectors and connoisseurs, The Au Bak Ling Collection Volume III marks the highly anticipated third dedicated sale of one of the most celebrated private collections of Chinese ceramics offered at Christie’s Hong Kong. The sale further underscores the longstanding trust placed in Christie’s by collectors and families stewarding some of the world’s most prestigious private collections. Presented during Christie’s 40th anniversary year in Asia, it brings together 40 exceptional masterpieces spanning the Song to Qing dynasties. Distinguished by their rarity, provenance, historical significance, and remarkable state of preservation, the masterpieces from The Au Bak Ling Collection stand as a testament to the

title: The Glyptotek opens world's first exhibition about power and fashion in the Roman Empire
summary: On 1 October 2026, the Glyptotek opens the largest special exhibition on antiquity in the museum’s history. Uniting the museum’s exceptional collection of Roman sculpture and unique loans from international museums, the exhibition shows the inextricable links between power and fashion that have existed for over 2,000 years. Opening this autumn, the Glyptotek’s exhibition The Power of Fashion in the Roman Empire will be the most ambitious to date on fashion in antiquity. Based on the museum’s long-standing research on colour and ancient dress and fashion, the exhibition presents the latest findings on the clothing, perfumes, jewellery and hairstyles those in power used to signal their position in the social hierarchy. Covering over 1,000 m2, The Power of Fashion in the Roman Empire is an exhibition that appeals to the senses. title: Kiang Malingue presents group exhibition Wayfarer of Fire in Hong Kong
summary: Kiang Malingue presents at its Hong Kong location Wayfarer of Fire, a group exhibition bringing together Brook Hsu, Kwan Sheung Chi, Lai Chih-Sheng, Phillip Lai, Ellen Pau, Apichatpong Weerasethakul, and Samson Young. With a focus on the transformative power of cinema, sound and labour, the artists turn to Promethean figures and revolutionary visions, tracing the ways in which individuals and communities act as keepers of the flame, collectors of cinders, and fire-watchers—tending the life-giving potential of fire, reflecting on its mobility, monumentality, and memory, setting amnesia ablaze. At the heart of the exhibition lies Ellen Pau’s single-channel video Blue (1989–90), a pivotal work that commemorates tragic historical events through a montage of war imagery. title: Christine Sun Kim explores communication and polarization in new MMCA exhibition
summary: MMCA×LG OLED Series is a mid-to-long-term partnership between the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea (MMCA) and LG Electronics that explores new possibilities in contemporary art. Each year, the project selects a single artist to present a newly commissioned site-specific work in Seoul Box, an iconic space at MMCA Seoul. Bringing together advanced display technology and artistic imagination, the series proposes a distinct mode of visual experience. MMCA×LG OLED Series 2026 presents Have Many Dumb Fights Against Rock by Christine Sun Kim. The exhibition introduces a large-scale digital animation alongside mural works that continues Kim’s ongoing inquiry into language and communication. The newly commissioned work actively engages both the architectural openness of Seoul Box and the spatial qualities of OLED

title: Gustaf Tenggren and Golden Age greats lead Heritage's $3.4 million Art of Disney Auction
summary: Three days of strong results spanning generations of Disney artistry drove Heritage’s Aug. 21-23 The Art of Disney Signature® Auction to $3.43 million. The event achieved a 100% sell-through rate across 1,346 lots and attracted 3,531 bidders from around the world. “This auction delivered strong results for Disney art from the studio’s Golden Age through the Disney Renaissance and into the films of the 2000s,” says Jim Lentz, Heritage Auctions’ Vice President of Animation and Anime Art. “The response reflects the global affection for Disney and the growing appreciation for animation art as a significant art form.” Gustaf Tenggren’s extraordinary concept paintings for Walt Disney’s groundbreaking 1937 feature Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs claimed the auction’s three highest results. title: Ben Brown Fine Arts to present Qi Lei solo exhibition Echoes of Day and Night
summary: Ben Brown Fine Arts will present Echoes of Day and Night, a solo exhibition of paintings by Qi Lei and the gallery’s first collaboration with the artist, who currently lives and works in Shanghai. Opening at the Hong Kong gallery on 12 September 2026 and running through 24 October, the exhibition brings together thirteen paintings created between 2020 and 2026. It marks Qi Lei’s first solo exhibition in Hong Kong since his debut solo presentation in the city in 2014. Echoes of Day and Night centres on Qi Lei’s recent reflections on music, painting and time. The title emerged from the artist seeing the post-rock band Godspeed You! Black Emperor perform live last year. Their music is highly abstract, seldom relying on lyrics or text, and builds its structure and rhythm through instrumental performance alone. title: Lafayette Anticipations to present Yu Nishimura, Hélène Fauquet and Mungo Thomson this fall
summary: Lafayette Anticipations has announced its autumn exhibition program, bringing together solo presentations by artists Yu Nishimura, Hélène Fauquet, and Mungo Thomson. Running concurrently, the lineup highlights three distinct artistic practices that examine memory, perception, and everyday material culture. From Nishimura’s dreamlike, marine-inspired paintings and Fauquet’s surreal sculptural investigations of photography to Thomson’s monumental subversions of analogue objects, the season offers a multifaceted exploration of contemporary landscape, form, and time. Lafayette Anticipations presents Towards a Sea, the first institutional solo exhibition in France by Japanese painter Yu Nishimura, born in 1982 in Kanagawa, where he still lives and works. title: Bath Preservation Trust appoints Spencer Hancock as Chief Operating Officer
summary: Following a major recruitment campaign, Bath Preservation Trust (BPT) has appointed Spencer Hancock as its first Chief Operating Officer. Spencer will be joining the charity in early September to take up this new role. Working closely with the Chief Executive and senior team, Spencer will provide operational leadership across BPT’s museums, ensuring an excellent visitor experience and overseeing day-to-day operations, facilities, commercial development, events and marketing. BPT runs four well-known museums in the World Heritage city of Bath, including No. 1 Royal Crescent, Beckford’s Tower and Museum, the Herschel Museum of Astronomy and the Museum of Bath Architecture. This new role has been created to ensure they continue to thrive and to grow. Spencer is well known in Bath having been the Head of Visitor Experience and Commercial

title: Fondazione Prada Film Fund: "The Difficult Bride" by Rubaiyat Hossain at the Venice Film Festival
summary: Rubaiyat Hossain’s The Difficult Bride, one of the projects supported by the first edition of Fondazione Prada Film Fund, has been selected to compete in the Orizzonti section of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. The film will have its world premiere on Sunday 6 September at 2.15 pm at Sala Darsena, Lido di Venezia. One year after its first call for entries, opened in September 2025 during the Venice Film Festival, Fondazione Prada Film Fund returns to Venice with one of the projects selected in its first edition. The Difficult Bride was chosen as one of 14 projects supported by the fund out of more than 1,200 applications received from around the world. title: Kestner Gesellschaft announces fall solo exhibitions by Min Yoon and Karimah Ashadu
summary: The Kestner Gesellschaft presents two solo exhibitions this fall, featuring the outstanding artists Min Yoon (b. 1986, Cheonan) and Karimah Ashadu (b. 1985, London). A Pronoun of B is the first comprehensive solo exhibition by Min Yoon. Born in South Korea and based in Vienna, Min Yoon works across drawing, painting, and sculpture to reflect on processes of artmaking and the institutional structures that shape art and its production. His work often expands into exuberant, multipart installations whose playful structures weave together a range of interests, contexts, and materials. The letter "B" in the title of the exhibition is believed to have evolved from an ancient Egyptian hieroglyph and a Proto-Sinaitic sign resembling the floor plan of a house. title: Autumn Knight explores the art of complaining in new ICA exhibition
summary: I Can’t Complain is a solo exhibition by New York-based artist Autumn Knight. Featuring a new commission alongside recent work, this is the first major presentation of her work in the UK. Knight’s interdisciplinary practice draws on theatre, psychology, improvisation and social exchange. Her exhibition at the ICA presents a new installation and performance work about the act of complaining: its pleasures, its frustrations, and its political potential. At a moment when questions of voice, authority, and participation are increasingly contested, I Can’t Complain opens a dialogue with audiences about how power is negotiated in everyday life, asking not how we can stop complaining, but what complaints make visible. title: Damien Jalet takes center stage as Cineteca Madrid opens new season
summary: Cineteca Madrid is opening its new season by looking beyond the traditional boundaries of cinema, bringing dance, music, digital art and expanded moving-image practices into the screening room throughout September. At the center of the month-long program is a tribute to French-Belgian choreographer Damien Jalet, whose work has increasingly moved between contemporary dance, film, music videos and the visual arts. Running from September 5 to 11 in collaboration with Centro Danza Matadero, the series brings together some of the films and projects that have helped make Jalet one of the most recognizable choreographic voices working across disciplines today. The program begins September 5 with Luca Guadagnino’s Suspiria (2018), a reimagining of the cult horror film in which dance functions as both ritual and hidden language.

title: NGV announces world-premiere exhibition Plant Life: The Nature of Design
summary: The NGV’s world-premiere exhibition, Plant Life: The Nature of Design, looks to the future of plant-based materials as a vital alternative to plastics, synthetic and non-renewable materials. From leather grown from fungi, to light-reactive bio-plastics, and fibreboard made from hemp and bio-resin, the exhibition features the work of leading designers using plant-based materials, including Formafantasma (Milan), Joris Laarman (Amsterdam), Crafting Plastics (Bratislava), EAST Architecture Studio (Beirut), alongside Australian practitioners Kate Scardifield, Ed Linacre, Broached Commissions and more. Presented thematically across four chapters and featuring more than 60 works, the exhibition brings together furniture, architecture, decorative arts, craft, photography and film drawn from the NGV Collection alongside a new commission by a bio-design

title: AGWA opens major exhibition of photography and video from South West Asia and North Africa
summary: The Art Gallery of Western Australia (AGWA) presents No night is long enough for us to dream twice, a major exhibition of contemporary photography and video, bringing together more than 100 works by seven living artists and one artist duo from across South West Asia, North Africa and its many diasporas. The exhibiting artists span the South West Asia North Africa (SWANA) region — including Algeria, Iran, Lebanon, Morocco, Palestine and Türkiye — with six artists presenting work in Australia for the first time, marking a significant moment of international exchange and visibility for these voices. No night is long enough for us to dream twice features the work of Basel Abbas (born 1983, Nicosia) and Ruanne Abou-Rahme (born 1983, Boston), Mohamad Abdouni (born 1989, Beirut), Hicham Benohoud (born 1968, Marrakech), Myriam Boulos

title: Heritage Auctions sets record with $63m sports collectibles sale
summary: Heritage Auctions’ Aug. 21-23 Summer Platinum Night Sports Auction rewrote the record books across the collecting world, realizing $62,963,254 — making it the largest sports auction ever held. The total broke the previous record for the world’s largest sports auction, set in 2024 when Heritage’s Summer Platinum Night Sports Auction, which featured the photo-matched jersey Babe Ruth wore when he hit his “Called Shot” home run in the 1932 World Series and achieved $61,645,972. “This was a landmark event for the entire sports-collecting hobby, bringing together extraordinary material from across generations and virtually every major collecting category,” says Chris Ivy, Heritage’s Director of Sports Auctions. “The record-setting auction total and more than 200 individual auction records reflect both the exceptional quality of the offerings

title: NASA Engineer's Rolex 'Paul Newman' Daytona lands in Heritage's Sept. 16 Watches & Fine Timepieces Auction
summary: A magnificent Rolex “Paul Newman” Cosmograph Daytona originally owned by a NASA engineer will reach the collecting market for the first time Sept. 16 in Heritage’s Watches & Fine Timepieces Signature® Auction. The Rolex Important & Rare Ref. 6239 “Paul Newman” Cosmograph Daytona, Circa 1969, one of 55 lots in the auction by the legendary watchmaker, was the personal watch of Oran W. Nicks, a pioneering aeronautical engineer and NASA leader known for directing lunar and planetary programs, and later leading Texas A&M University’s Low-Speed Wind Tunnel that now bears his name. “This is an exceptional watch that comes directly from the family of the original owner,” says Jim Wolf, Heritage’s

title: National Gallery of Armenia presents Karen Ohanyan solo exhibition Delicate Matter
summary: The National Gallery of Armenia, in collaboration with Atamian Hovsepian Curatorial Practice, presents Delicate Matter, an exhibition of recent works by Karen Ohanyan, curated by Tamar Hovsepian. The exhibition is organized within the framework of Prospectations, the National Gallery of Armenia's programme highlighting contemporary Armenian art. The works are co-commissioned by Sharjah Art Foundation and Atamian Hovsepian Curatorial Practice. Following their presentation in Armenia, the works will be exhibited as part of Sharjah Biennial 17: What Remains, sits restive, on view in Sharjah, UAE, from January 21 to June 17, 2027.​ Delicate Matter unfolds through the multiple meanings of the word matter. It refers to the delicate matters we often avoid naming—questions of power, masculinity, violence, and vulnerability—and to matter
